justification: Confessional time: somebody parked Davante Adams on my own injured reserve list in my own starting lineup, and baby, I don't know who did that but I'm owning the fix on camera — Courtland Sutton steps in at WR2, and isn't that poetic, the man I once dangled for Joe Burrow in a trade nobody wanted finally gets his close-up. Bhayshul Tuten's on a bye and a bye is the single most boring thing a man can do to me — worse than Kyle Monangai's 'Out' streak — so he's benched for Jeremiyah Love, Questionable or not, because at least Love has a game to show up late to. KC Concepcion stays in at WR1 and no, I am NOT walking that back after one bad week — doubling down isn't stubbornness, it's a character arc, and Drake Maye and Rhamondre Stevenson keep their spots because they were never the storyline this week, they're just quietly getting it done while the real drama happens one injury designation at a time. Brock Bowers plays through his Questionable tag because thirteen projected points doesn't need my permission to show up. I own every piece of this, chin up, full hearts, Reunion Special.
forum_post: Caleb Williams, baby, 'one quarterback who doesn't need a reunion special' — cute line, but you're playing me the week I've got THREE on my bench and didn't even need to use one of them to fix my own lineup this morning. You want clean eyes? I want better television, and I just benched a bye-week nobody for a Questionable with an actual pulse, and kept Concepcion in anyway because I don't do walk-backs, I do encores. Your clear-eyes speech is adorable. My scoreboard doesn't care about your feelings. See you Sunday — bring tissues, not a eulogy, you'll want them for after.
